newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty flat vs basket, 1-day depos inch lower.
newsitem.headline: Zloty flat vs basket, 1-day depos inch lower.

text.p: The zloty held flat against the parity rate in early Wednesday trade and was seen idle for the rest of the day as foreign investors left the zloty alone after pounding it down two percent last week, dealers said.
"The market is very quiet and there are no foreign players active giving the zloty a breather after its sharp fall," said Malgorzta Sawicka, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 0.46/0.41 percent above the parity rate against 0.47/0.32 percent at the opening and seen stable at around the 0.40 percent level for the day.
It was at 3.2330/45 against the dollar and 1.8975/85 against the mark against 3.2285/350 and 1.8990/20 respectively.
"The market is likely to stew in its own sauce with no clear direction for a while because foreigners are on the sidelines," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at ING bank.
In the longer term, however, dealers expected the zloty to rise because of good Polish fundamentals, which are likely to draw foreign investors back to Poland.
On the money market one-day deposit rates edged 0.4 point lower at offer to 23.50/25.10 percent since morning while tomorrow/next offers were flat at 23.90/25.50 percent.
"The market is tight because banks are squaring reserve positions before the end of the reserve on Sunday," said Marta Kepa of Pekao SA.
Thursday is Corpus Christi holiday in Poland.
The National Bank of Poland offered to drain 250 million zlotys from the market through a sale of its 91-day bills, maturing August 27 with today's value date.
